issues.description: Differential validation shows the expert golden solution is REJECTED by evaluate.py (exit code 1, FR2/FR4/SR3 all fail with cycle mismatches), meaning the reference netlist behavior encoded in the golden RTL does not match the actual simulated flattened_netlist.v output. This indicates either the golden solution incorrectly implements the '1011' detector, or the flattened_netlist.v gate logic (which is convoluted and contains suspicious placeholder/unused wires like n19_dup, m2b, and ad-hoc De Morgan chains) does not actually implement the documented '1011' non-overlapping detector semantics described in the ground_truth and design comments.
issues.evidence: golden_run: [TEST] FAIL: FR2: output mismatch on 2/30 cycles; FAIL: FR4: mismatch on 7/65 cycles; FAIL: SR3: mismatch on 1/12 cycles

issues.description: Since the golden run fails, the benchmark case is unusable as-is: there is no verified-correct submission that passes the grader, so mutation_score is meaningless (0.0) and coverage cannot be trusted.

The netlist contains structurally suspicious/inconsistent gate wiring (e.g., the next-state logic for s1 seems to omit a term for 'from_start_1', and comments contradict actual gate connections in several places), suggesting the netlist itself may not faithfully implement the stated non-overlapping '1011' Moore detector, which is the root cause of the golden/vulnerable both failing FR2/FR4/SR3.
issues.evidence: Both golden_run and vulnerable_run fail FR2 with mismatches on the shipped stimulus, which should only happen if the reference oracle disagrees with any correct implementation of the documented behavior.

recommendations: Re-derive the flattened_netlist.v gate-level logic to ensure it actually implements the documented non-overlapping '1011' Moore detector; verify via an independent reference simulation before shipping.
Fix the golden/recovered_rtl.v (or the netlist) so that the golden solution passes FR2, FR4, and SR3 against the actual reference netlist simulation.
Re-run the differential check after correcting the mismatch and confirm golden_run exits 0 while a naive/empty baseline still exits non-zero.

Add an internal consistency test (e.g., a reference Python/behavioral model compared against the gate netlist simulation) during benchmark authoring to catch such netlist/golden divergences before publishing.
